# Power storage Because of [textlink="grid ramping" link="Ramping"], station power consumption is rarely steady. Energy storage smooths out brief dips and spikes and buys time when generation temporarily cannot meet demand.
Every transformer ([color=orange]HV[/color], [color=yellow]MV[/color], [color=green]LV[/color]) has a small buffer, but SMES units are needed to keep an entire station sector running.
## Basic SMES Superconducting Magnetic Energy Storage (SMES) receives [color=orange]HV[/color] through a cable terminal and supplies power to the grid through the cable beneath it.
The terminal separates the input and output so the two lines do not connect to each other.
A basic SMES stores [color=orange][protodata="SMESBasic" comp="Battery" member="MaxCharge" format="N0"/] J[/color] and can supply up to [color=orange][protodata="SMESBasic" comp="PowerNetworkBattery" member="MaxSupply" format="N0"/] W[/color].
## Advanced SMES An upgraded model for station power arrays and longer operation during generation shortfalls.
An advanced SMES stores [color=orange][protodata="SMESAdvanced" comp="Battery" member="MaxCharge" format="N0"/] J[/color] and supplies up to [color=orange][protodata="SMESAdvanced" comp="PowerNetworkBattery" member="MaxSupply" format="N0"/] W[/color].
## Extended SMES A large Sunrise storage unit for high-power sections of the grid.
An extended SMES stores [color=orange][protodata="SMESExtended" comp="Battery" member="MaxCharge" format="N0"/] J[/color] and supplies up to [color=orange][protodata="SMESExtended" comp="PowerNetworkBattery" member="MaxSupply" format="N0"/] W[/color].
## Super-extended SMES Sunrise's top-tier storage unit for extremely heavy grids and long-term backup power.
A super-extended SMES stores [color=orange][protodata="SMESSuperExtended" comp="Battery" member="MaxCharge" format="N0"/] J[/color] and supplies up to [color=orange][protodata="SMESSuperExtended" comp="PowerNetworkBattery" member="MaxSupply" format="N0"/] W[/color].
Even the highest-capacity SMES cannot replace generation: if total demand consistently exceeds production, the batteries will still run dry.
